methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a seed-stage ocean and maritime frontier-tech company founded by Christopher Amidon. The company has raised $10M+ to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in the ocean and maritime sector (Clippership, NetworkOcean, Albacore); no direct public comparables exist in this nascent domain.

The valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, the primary applicable technique given limited data density at the seed stage. Using total raised ($10M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied value of $25M. This single-method triangulation produces a valuation range of $21M (low) to $29M (high), with a median of $25M.

The analysis supports a valuation in the $21M–$29M range, centered on $25M. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for the ocean and maritime sector specifically, limited visibility into private comparable valuations, and the absence of public market reference points. The reliance on a single valuation method and the early stage of the company constrain conviction in precision. Deeper analysis would require transaction multiples from the three identified private peers and clearer articulation of Standard Subsea's differentiated technology and market position within the ocean tech ecosystem.
